reasoning: Since this is the first round, I'll accept the report's changes as largely sound and prepare concrete edits with exact quotes: replacing the full target_cube and picks_done descriptions, updating the memory policy prompts, and revising the holding test subgoal with its fallback, required count, and pointing logic.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for two times' means 2 pick-ups.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for two times' means 2 pick-ups; 'three times' means 3 pick-ups.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: - If the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%) and the cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list, the robot is holding the cube: choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open, all cubes on the table):
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: - The robot is holding the cube if and only if the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%); the cube list is irrelevant to this test (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position), and fingers 100% open means not holding regardless of any 'lifted off the table' line. Holding: choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open):

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: If a situation matches no rule (for example the gripper state is ambiguous or target_cube cannot be matched to any listed cube), prefer: holding something -> B; not holding and picks_done below the requirement -> A at the cube nearest target_cube; else -> C. Never point at any cube other than the one nearest target_cube.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: If the execution steps shown include a descent to table height (gripper below about 0.04), point at the listed cube nearest that descent position; it is the same cube as target_cube. Pointing at the listed cube position, or within a few px of it (such as the demonstration's grasp position), is acceptable. Never point at any cube other than the one nearest target_cube.

edits.modify_from: Position [y, x] of the cube to pick. At the first decision step (memory empty), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS: find the cube that appears as 'held in the gripper' (or disappears from the table list while the gripper fingers are about 46% open), note where it was on the table just before the gripper came down on it, and write the position of the cube that sits closest to that spot in the scene at the start of execution (the cube is set down and the shuffle returns it to nearly the same place). At every later step, if the scene at this decision step lists a cube on the table within about 10 px of the carried value, write that cube's current position; if the cube is currently held in the gripper, copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. [93, 140]
edits.modify_to: Position [y, x] of the cube to pick: the one the demonstration grasped. At the first decision step (memory empty): find the demonstration frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) with fingers about 46-51% open; the grasped cube is the listed cube (from a frame before the gripper descended) nearest that gripper position, and it is the one reported 'held in the gripper' in the following frames. Ignore cubes that vanish from the list earlier while the gripper is high and 100% open; they are only hidden by the arm. After the put-down, follow that cube through every remaining demonstration frame: in each frame it is the listed cube nearest its position in the previous frame (cubes swap places during the shuffle and move tens of pixels per frame, and lists are sorted by y, not identity; do not assume it returns to its old spot). Write the position of the cube in the scene at the start of execution nearest its last demonstration position. At every later decision step: if the execution steps shown include a frame with the gripper at table height (below about 0.04), write the position, in the scene at this decision step, of the listed cube nearest that lowest gripper position (that cube was just picked or just set down, and it is the target); otherwise copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. [85, 109]

edits.modify_from: At any later step, look at the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step): if the gripper is raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%) and a cube is held in the gripper or missing from the table list, write the carried value plus one; otherwise write the carried value unchanged. e.g. 1
edits.modify_to: At any later step, look only at the gripper in the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step): if it is raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), write the carried value plus one, no matter what the cube list says (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position); if the fingers are 100% open, copy the carried value unchanged even if a cube line says 'lifted off the table'. e.g. 1

edits.modify_from: Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked up: the cube that is listed as 'held in the gripper' (or vanishes from the table list while the gripper is closed) during the DEMONSTRATION STEPS, located where it sits on the table in the scene at the start of execution (it is set back down at nearly the spot it was lifted from, and the shuffle at the end of the demonstration returns it there). At every later step the value is refreshed to the current table position of that same cube (the listed cube nearest the previous value, within about 10 px) whenever it is resting on the table; while the cube is held in the gripper the value is left unchanged. e.g. [93, 140]
edits.modify_to: Current table position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration grasped. At the first decision step the grasped cube is identified as the listed cube (from a demonstration frame before the gripper descended) nearest the gripper's position in the demonstration frame where the gripper is at its lowest (height about 0.02) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%), confirmed by the first frame that lists a cube 'held in the gripper'; cubes that vanish from the list earlier while the gripper is still high and 100% open are merely occluded by the arm and are not the grasped cube. That cube is then followed frame by frame to the end of the demonstration by nearest-neighbour matching (each cube goes to the listed position closest to its previous one, conflicts resolved by the smallest total displacement; cubes swap places during the shuffle and move tens of pixels per frame, and lists are sorted by y, not identity, so the cube is not assumed to return to its old spot). Its position in the last demonstration frame, matched to the nearest listed cube in the scene at the start of execution, is the value. At every later decision step: if the execution steps since the previous decision step include a frame where the gripper is at table height (height below about 0.04), the value becomes the listed position, in the scene at this decision step, of the cube nearest that lowest gripper position (the cube just picked or just put down, which is the same cube); otherwise the carried value is copied. e.g. [85, 109]

edits.modify_from: It goes up by one at each decision step whose own scene (the last frame) shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers partly closed on the cube (about 46% open, cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list). edits.modify_to: It goes up by one at each decision step whose own scene (the last frame) shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), regardless of what the cube list says (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position; a 'held in the gripper' line in the execution steps is corroborating but not required). revision.refused: The proposed field recording the previous command is not added: the corrected holding test (fingers 46-51% versus 100% open, cube list ignored) settles the 'lifted off the table' ambiguity from what the step shows, so the field would fail NECESSITY. No separate rule is added for choosing between the demonstration's grasp position and the cube's listed position, since both select the same cube and either is now stated as acceptable. The request to count picks of a cube other than target_cube is not committed as a separate rule: the count already increments on the gripper state alone, regardless of which cube was grasped, and the corrected target_cube removes the situation.
